rationale: PINS the use-list import module/items contract (#261 wave 3, found 2026-08-28): pre-fix `use std::io::{Read, Write as W}` stored module="std::io::{Read, Write as W}" with comma-split garbage items, violating the family contract (JS/Java: module = path prefix, items = local bindings). Alias-aware: `Write as W` binds W. Wildcard imports emit items=["*"]. RSD6 pins (2026-09-05): a NESTED group `use std::{env, io, path::{Path, PathBuf}}` binds Path/PathBuf (65 such declarations dropped them across cargo+ripgrep) and stays a single std row; a TOP-LEVEL group `use {std::sync::Arc, ...}` has no shared prefix — each binding becomes its OWN row with its full module path (pre-fix fabricated module 'Read, File'; 28 declarations). Not covered by the differential oracle (imports are fixture-gated only), so these pins are the sole regression guards. RUST-D25 adds the ABSOLUTE path forms: `use ::libc::c_int;` published module `libc::libc::c_int` because a leading-`::` scoped_identifier has no `path` field and the namedChild(0) fallback used the name as its own prefix. The doubled segment is forbidden here so the regression cannot return silently. RUST-D27 adds a MULTI-LINE top-level group: every row used to take the range of the whole `use` declaration, so all three pointed at the `use {` line, which bears none of the three paths. The three pins below name the FULL range object because that is the only falsifiable form of a line assertion — the html #888 precedent is that identity comparison makes a range pin silently unmatchable, and an unmatchable pin proves nothing. RUST-D29: a comment or stray separator inside a use tree is not a module path. The collector's fallback accepted ANY node and published its raw text, so `use {a ,, b}` published module `,` and `use {/* c */ Foo}` published the comment. Narrowing that fallback to path-bearing nodes then broke `crate::foo::{...}`, whose path field is a `crate` NODE rather than an identifier, and the module became `::foo` — the narrower rule CREATED the second defect, on the same run, which is why the forbids below pin both halves rather than trusting either.

expectImports.comment: RSD6a: nested-group leaves are bound, module stays the outer prefix
RSD6b: top-level group -> one row per binding
RUST-D27: line 22 is the path itself, not the `use {` on line 20
RUST-D27: the group binds the inner leaves; the range is the whole bstr::{B, ByteSlice} path
RUST-D29: a comment next to a real binding is not itself one
RUST-D29: crate is a path ROOT node; narrowing the fallback must not lose the prefix

RUST-D29: super is a path ROOT node. Module is the full path INCLUDING the leaf, per the convention every other row in this fixture follows — my first pin wrote the prefix alone and the fixture was right to reject it.

forbidImports.comment: RSD6b: the fabricated joined-items module must never return
RUST-D25: a leading :: must not be read as a path segment and doubled
RUST-D25: same defect one segment deeper
RUST-D29: a separator is not a module
RUST-D29: a comment is not a module
RUST-D29: the crate prefix was lost, leaving a leading :: — the narrower rule's own regression
